overview: Land’s End is the far western tip of mainland England, where granite cliffs drop straight into the Atlantic. It’s one of those places most people want to tick off at least once, and on a clear, breezy day standing on the clifftops looking out to sea is genuinely exhilarating. Look out for Wolf Rock lighthouse on the horizon.

Be ready for two different sides to it. Behind the cliffs is a privately run visitor complex with a hotel, cafés, shops, the famous signpost and some paid family attractions. But the 110 acres of protected clifftop around it are free to walk and open all year, so you can skip the commercial bit entirely and just go for a walk.

expect.title: Cliff walks
expect.text: Signed paths run along the clifftops, and the coast path heads north towards Sennen. The rocks formed around 270 million years ago, which explains the jagged, dramatic coastline.

expect.title: Seabird spotting
expect.text: Gannets, fulmars, kittiwakes, shags and razorbills are all regulars, and if you’re lucky you might see a Cornish chough. Pack the binoculars.

expect.title: Family attractions
expect.text: One ticket covers four attractions: an indoor 15-hole adventure golf course, a walk-through Aardman exhibit, a 4D film and a small farm with animals. They’re closed over winter and reopen in spring.

expect.title: The signpost
expect.text: The famous Land’s End signpost is a paid photo experience, so expect a queue in summer if you want the classic shot.

goodToKnow.label: Parking
goodToKnow.text: Parking is paid, and the money helps look after the protected landscape. Check the website for current arrangements and the locals’ discount.

goodToKnow.label: Opening
goodToKnow.text: The coast paths never close. The attractions, cafés and shops keep shorter hours, shut for maintenance in winter, and can be affected by bad weather.

goodToKnow.label: Food
goodToKnow.text: There’s a café overlooking the farm and the sea, a kiosk for pasties and ice cream, picnic benches, and a hotel restaurant and bar.

setting.note: Clifftop walks plus indoor family attractions

kids.note: Family attractions including a farm and adventure golf

week.slot: An hour or two (more with the attractions)
week.text: Land’s End fits neatly into a day exploring the far west. An hour on the headland is plenty if you’re just here for the view and a short walk; add a couple more if the children want the attractions. Wind and sea spray make it much more dramatic, so a blowy day can be a good time to go.

pairWith.why: a big sandy beach, walkable along the cliffs
for a swim in clear water on the south side

tips: If you’re fit, walk in along the coast path from Sennen Cove rather than driving, and treat the visitor centre as your halfway café stop.
Bring a windproof layer even on a sunny day: it’s exposed out on the point.
Go late in the day in summer for fewer people and the sun dropping over the sea.
